To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
(1) weather shocks have persistent, positive effects on land values; and (2) these effects are stronger for farms with higher debt and for farms in low income counties.

(i) weather shocks have persistent and amplified effects on land values; (ii) the effects of weather shocks on land values are larger during the farm crisis of the 80s and in low-income counties; (iii) weather shocks lead to higher farm investment and lower borrowing; and (iv) the effects of shocks are stronger for farms that have more debt.

(1) past weather shocks have significant and persistent effects on land prices and productivity up to three years after the initial shock; and (2) the effects of weather shocks are significantly larger during the 1980’s farm debt crisis.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the propagation and amplification of shocks to land values and productivity.
the transmission of shocks in the real sector of the economy and their effects on financial variables.
the propagation and amplification of exogenous productivity shocks in agriculture.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
weather shocks have significant effects on agricultural output and land values, and these effects are magnified in the presence of financial market frictions.
financial accelerators are indeed at work, but that the effects are more complex than previously assumed.
weather shocks have persistent and amplifying effects on land values, productivity, and investment.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the financial accelerator is at work in agriculture.
weather shocks are propagated through the agricultural production function and amplified through the financial accelerator.
weather shocks have a significant effect on land prices, which in turn affect future productivity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the financial accelerator is alive and well in agriculture, and that it is particularly active during economic downturns and in areas of the country where credit is scarce.
the financial accelerator can be empirically tested using a novel dataset.
financial accelerator models can help explain the transmission of weather shocks into the future.
